title: Mechanism for Zincophilic Sites on Zinc-Metal Anode Hosts in Aqueous Batteries

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: How zincophilic sites govern zinc nucleation and deposition on carbon anode hosts is not established. Resorcinol-formaldehyde-derived carbon hollow spheres (C HS) chosen as the model zinc-metal-anode host.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (DES/base_system), n3 (PRC/synthesis), n4 (PRC/stimulus), n7 (HYP/hypothesis), n8 (DES/method), n10 (DES/down_select), n11a (PRC/synthesis). Premises: The distribution of initial nuclei governs subsequent zinc deposition and cell performance (refs 36,37,41,45,46)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Plated zinc coexists on the carbon host as dispersed single atoms, ~1 nm clusters and extended porous networks. Nitrogen is incorporated into the shell of CnC HS and is absent in C HS.
states.detail: Absorbed: n6 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n11 (STR/chemistry/composition), n12 (STR/chemistry/bonding), n14 (STR/microstructure/shape). Premises: In N 1s NEXAFS the 398.1 eV feature is pyridinic nitrogen and the 401.1 eV feature graphitic nitrogen, with pyrrolic overlapping; A Raman band near 1200 cm-1 is characteristic of pyridine; the 1580 cm-1 G band serves as the graphitic-carbon normalisation reference

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Zinc adsorbs as single atoms that seed clusters, which expand into a mesoporous zinc network. The distribution of initial nucleation sites induces the subsequent zinc deposition and sets electrochemical performance.
states.detail: Absorbed: n5 (MEC/pathway), n20 (MEC/pathway), n9 (PRP/value), n13 (MEC/identification), n15 (MEC/pathway), n16 (PRP/value). Premises: The distribution of initial nuclei governs subsequent zinc deposition and cell performance (refs 36,37,41,45,46)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: CnC HS sustains ~200 plating/stripping cycles and >7000 min symmetric cycling, while C HS fails near 50 cycles and ~4400 min

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: The mechanism of zincophilic sites is Zn-N bond formation at pyridinic nitrogen, which spreads nucleation and suppresses zinc dendrites

nodes.title: MICRO, F3
nodes.head: Zinc on CnC HS is a largely flat deposit with sparse protruding platelets; on C HS the surface is a dense mat of sharp platelets
nodes.solves: Plated zinc is planar and compact on CnC HS but forms a dense mat of sharp dendritic platelets on C HS
nodes.note: both panels carry a 10 um bar; panel d still shows scattered sharp protrusions, so 'most of the zinc is planar' holds but a dendrite-free surface does not

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: N 1s NEXAFS shows sharp features near 398 and 401 eV for CnC HS and none for C HS
nodes.solves: Nitrogen is incorporated into the shell of CnC HS and is absent in C HS
nodes.note: the C HS trace is a featureless rising background over 380-420 eV; the two traces are vertically offset
nodes.detail: o10: N 1s NEXAFS shows sharp features near 398 and 401 eV for CnC HS and none for C HS
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n11 (o10).

nodes.title: ECHEM:LSV, RAMAN, F3
nodes.head: After zinc deposition the ~398 eV N 1s feature collapses and the ~401 eV feature becomes the taller of the two. The ~1200 cm-1 Raman feature weakens from the pristine trace at the top of the stack to the zinc-loaded trace at the bottom.
nodes.solves: On zinc plating Zn-N bonds form at pyridinic-nitrogen sites, moving their chemical state toward graphitic nitrogen
nodes.op: compare across conditions, cross check consistency
nodes.note: the ranking reversal is robust to the vertical offset between the two traces; shaded bands mark 396.5-399.5 and 400-402 eV linked text: the four traces are successive LSV scans and all spectra are normalised to the G band; the panel itself labels only the top (pristine) and bottom (with zinc) traces; x-axis ticks read 1200/1350/1500/1650 cm-1, the packet OCR gives 1850 for the last the D (~1345) and G (~1590) bands are far above noise; the shaded 1180-1240 cm-1 window shows no peak clearly separable from the baseline ripple in any trace
nodes.detail: o11: After zinc deposition the ~398 eV N 1s feature collapses and the ~401 eV feature becomes the taller of the two; o13: The ~1200 cm-1 Raman feature weakens from the pristine trace at the top of the stack to the zinc-loaded trace at the bottom; a2: In all four Raman traces the ~1200 cm-1 window lies within the trace noise, so the claimed decrease is not resolved above it
nodes.inner_audit: a2: the D (~1345) and G (~1590) bands are far above noise; the shaded 1180-1240 cm-1 window shows no peak clearly separable from the baseline ripple in any trace
nodes.necessity_reason: Changes support for S1: o13 partial

nodes.solves: Zinc adsorbs as single atoms that seed clusters, which expand into a mesoporous zinc network
nodes.note: F1b marks the small features with red arrows and the extended ones with green arrows; F1c shows the three scales at 1 nm, 2 nm and 2 nm, the third with resolved fringes

nodes.title: ATOM, F2
nodes.head: Electron accumulation sits as a detached lobe above zinc on pristine graphene but is denser in the zinc-substrate gap on N-doped graphene
nodes.solves: Zinc adsorption is exothermic on N-doped graphene (-0.072 to -0.089 eV) but endothermic on pristine graphene (+0.014 to +0.030 eV)
nodes.necessity_reason: n9 keeps shown support from o22, o5, o7 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: The N-doped cell shows a localised charge hotspot at the nitrogen, absent at the equivalent site of the pristine cell. Annotated Bader charges are -1.1741 e at the nitrogen site N1 and 0.0036 e at the equivalent carbon site.
nodes.op: assess spatial distribution, read characteristic point
nodes.note: apart from the small red/yellow spot at N1 the two honeycomb maps look identical the panel's colour bar runs 0 to 0.6 and cannot represent the quoted -1.1741 e, so the number is taken from the written annotation, not from the map the panel carries only a small 'N' label; speckle is at the level expected for a low-count map
nodes.detail: o4: The N-doped cell shows a localised charge hotspot at the nitrogen, absent at the equivalent site of the pristine cell; o22: Annotated Bader charges are -1.1741 e at the nitrogen site N1 and 0.0036 e at the equivalent carbon site; o9: The nitrogen map fills the sphere shell evenly, with no clustering or radial gradient
nodes.necessity_reason: n9, n15 keeps shown support from o5, o6, o7 after removal.

nodes.title: ATOM:DFT, XPS, F2
nodes.head: Charge transfer to zinc is more negative at every N-doped site (-0.032 to -0.037 e) than at the pristine sites (-0.023 to -0.027 e). Binding energies are +0.030/+0.014/+0.029 eV at top/hollow/bridge on pristine graphene and -0.072/-0.089/-0.077 eV on N-doped graphene
nodes.solves: Zinc adsorption is exothermic on N-doped graphene (-0.072 to -0.089 eV) but endothermic on pristine graphene (+0.014 to +0.030 eV)
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: on N-doped graphene the top site transfers the most (~-0.037 e), not the hollow site; the axis is truncated at -0.02 so the bars do not start from zero panel citation dropped: crop F2d carries OCR cue class 'XPS' from its 'Binding Energy (eV)' axis label, which is incompatible with ATOM:DFT; values read from the bar chart in the whole-figure image
nodes.detail: o5: Charge transfer to zinc is more negative at every N-doped site (-0.032 to -0.037 e) than at the pristine sites (-0.023 to -0.027 e); o7: Binding energies are +0.030/+0.014/+0.029 eV at top/hollow/bridge on pristine graphene and -0.072/-0.089/-0.077 eV on N-doped graphene
nodes.necessity_reason: n9 keeps shown support from o22, o6 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F3
nodes.head: The sharp 290.1 eV C 1s feature of pristine CnC HS is absent after zinc deposition, while the 284.9 and 288.3 eV features remain
nodes.solves: Pyridinic nitrogen, rather than graphitic nitrogen or bare graphitic carbon, is the electrochemically active zincophilic site
nodes.note: in the zinc-loaded trace a broad sigma* step near 292.5 eV replaces the sharp 290.1 eV peak
nodes.detail: o12: The sharp 290.1 eV C 1s feature of pristine CnC HS is absent after zinc deposition, while the 284.9 and 288.3 eV features remain
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n13 (o12).

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: The two hosts' plating plateaus nearly coincide at the lowest rate and separate strongly at the highest (about -0.05 V vs -0.10 V). Nucleation overpotentials of 39 mV and 43 mV are marked on the two initial discharge profiles
nodes.solves: CnC HS lowers the zinc nucleation overpotential (39 vs 43 mV) and the plating overpotential at every current density
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: the three sub-panels are labelled 0.5/2.0/4.0 mA h cm-2 although caption and linked text call them current densities in mA cm-2; at the middle rate the axis reads about 45 vs 55 mV against the text's 36 vs 52 mV the packet's annotations list for F4d omits the in-plot strings '39mV' and '43mV' although both appear in its OCR tokens; the two curves are drawn in near-identical dark colours so the arrows cannot be assigned from the panel alone
nodes.detail: o17: The two hosts' plating plateaus nearly coincide at the lowest rate and separate strongly at the highest (about -0.05 V vs -0.10 V); o18: Nucleation overpotentials of 39 mV and 43 mV are marked on the two initial discharge profiles
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n16 (o18).

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: CnC HS holds roughly 93-100% Coulombic efficiency to about 205 cycles; C HS data end near 50 cycles after falling to zero at ~40 and ~48. The two Coulombic-efficiency records span very different lengths (about 50 vs 205 cycles), so the quoted average efficiencies cover unequal ranges.
nodes.solves: CnC HS sustains ~200 plating/stripping cycles and >7000 min symmetric cycling, while C HS fails near 50 cycles and ~4400 min
nodes.op: compare across conditions, cross check consistency
nodes.note: the text's ~93% (C HS) vs ~95% (CnC HS) averages cannot be separated by eye; both series are open circles differing only in colour, and the first C HS point sits near 77% over the shared 1-50 cycle window the two series are indistinguishable by eye apart from the C HS dropouts the linked text puts the hysteresis increase after 3000 min and the fluctuation after 4000 min; the plot shows the first large spikes at about 2600-3000 min the right-hand current-density trace steps up at about 1800, 2400 and 3000 min
nodes.detail: o15: CnC HS holds roughly 93-100% Coulombic efficiency to about 205 cycles; C HS data end near 50 cycles after falling to zero at ~40 and ~48; a3: The two Coulombic-efficiency records span very different lengths (about 50 vs 205 cycles), so the quoted average efficiencies cover unequal ranges; o16: C HS voltage spikes grow from ~2600 min and its trace ends near 4400 min at the 'C HS battery failure' arrow, while CnC HS stays within ~0.03 V to 7100 min; o19: Under a stepped current-density staircase C HS develops large voltage spikes from ~2300 min while CnC HS stays within ~0.05 V to 3500 min
nodes.inner_audit: a3: over the shared 1-50 cycle window the two series are indistinguishable by eye apart from the C HS dropouts
nodes.necessity_reason: Changes support for S3: o15 partial

nodes.head: Charge and discharge capacity fall from about 1.0 to about 0.9 mAh over 500 cycles and the 1st and 100th cycle profiles nearly overlap. A cell stack wired to a multimeter powers a switched-on mobile phone
